author: Floyd O. Ingram
title: 2026 Bell County Crops Conference - NewsBreak
text:
By Floyd O. Ingram ,
7 hours ago Seaton Star Hall, 10842 Highway 53, Temple, Texas, will host the 2026 Bell County Crops Conference on Wednesday, Jan. 14. Registration begins at 7:30 a.m., and the program will start at 8 a.m. The program will conclude at 2:30 p.m.
For years, the Bell County Crops Conference has provided pertinent, up-todate education on new technologies, best management practices, and strategies to increase crop yield and profit margins. Breakfast will be provided by Capital Farm Credit, and lunch will be catered by Johnny’s Steaks & BBQ.
The conference offers five hours of CEUs (1 – Laws & Regulations, 2 – IPM, and 2 – General) for renewal of private applicator licenses and certificate holders. The conference will also include the 2026 Auxin Specific Applicator Training for the use of approved Dicamba and 2,4-D herbicides for licensed and non-licensed applicators.
Speakers and topics include: “2026 Auxin Herbicide Training & Statewide Cotton Overview” – Dr. Benjamin McKnight “Commodity & Livestock Market Update & Outlook” – Dr. Jason Johnson “Farm Management Considerations for 2026” – Dr. Ronnie Schnell “TDA Pesticide Laws & Regulations” – Dr. Don Renchie “New World Screwworm Update from Texas Animal Health Commission” – T.R. Lansford III, D.V.M., Texas Animal Health Commission deputy executive director “IPM Strategies in Row Crop Entomology” – Tyler Mays As in past years, the conference will host an industry trade show with vendors such as Ag Southwest, BASF, BH Genetics, Bayer Crop Science, Capital Farm Credit, Clearwater UWCD, Corteva, Croprotek, Evans Ranch, Georgia Pirtle Crop Insurance, LG Seeds, Dekalb, Lonestar Ag Credit, Marek Ag, Martinez Spraying, Pioneer, Schaeffer Manufacturing, Shepard Crop Insurance, Texas Corn Producers, Texas Wheat, WC Tractor, Wilbur-Ellis, and many more. Door prizes and special offers from these vendors will be drawn at the conclusion of the day.
